checkpoints.description: [1/4] Scaffold driftwood package, git churn parser and baseline tests

impact_assessment.why: A maintainer needs an offline signal for where refactoring pays off, built from local git history only.
impact_assessment.benefits: Ranked hotspot report with reproducible scores and a unit-test shield for every metric.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new project, no public API yet; dependency: stdlib only, no third-party packages; concurrency: none, single-process CLI; state: read-only over the target repository, no writes.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep every metric a small pure function with its own test; CLI is the only side-effecting layer.

handoff.evidence: aikit new created project at projects/driftwood

checkpoints.description: [milestone 4/4] CLI, report, README and tests delivered; checklists: passed
[1/3] Review hardening: fix flat-metric scoring, CLI validation and dead code; add real-git integration tests

impact_assessment.why: The first delivery had a scoring edge case, unvalidated numeric flags, dead helper code and only mocked git coverage.
impact_assessment.benefits: Correct scores for small repos, exit-2 argument errors, verified rename/history parsing against real git, 37 green tests.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Hotspot score semantics for flat metrics change; dependency: none added; concurrency: none; state: read-only over target repos.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Documented the saturation rule in README and covered it plus the CLI validation with tests.

handoff.next: run gates, commit and publish driftwood
